guarantees.claim: mux_err is initialized to no error: valid=0, code=ErrNone, info=0.
When mux_sel_buf_err_check is not SelSw and sw_valid_i is high, mux_err is driven with valid=1, code=ErrSwPushedMsgFifo, and info containing st and mux_sel_buf_err_check.
When app_active_o is high and sw_cmd_i is not CmdNone, mux_err is driven with valid=1, code=ErrSwIssuedCmdInAppActive, and info=sw_cmd_i.

assumptions.claim: sw_cmd_i must be CmdNone when sw_valid_i is deasserted.
assumptions.risk: If violated, the block will incorrectly assert ErrSwIssuedCmdInAppActive, potentially triggering false fault reactions.

uncertain_points.claim: When both error conditions (mux_sel_buf_err_check != SelSw && sw_valid_i) and (app_active_o && sw_cmd_i != CmdNone) are true simultaneously, only the first error is reported. It is unclear if this priority encoding is intentional or if the second error should also be recorded.
uncertain_points.risk: SW command violation during app active may be missed if a FIFO push error occurs at the same time.

uncertain_points.claim: sw_cmd_i is checked independently of sw_valid_i. If sw_cmd_i can hold a value other than CmdNone when sw_valid_i is low, the block will spuriously assert ErrSwIssuedCmdInAppActive.
uncertain_points.cond: app_active_o is high and sw_valid_i is low
uncertain_points.risk: Spurious error assertion could lead to false fault handling, denial-of-service, or incorrect security response.
